title: What are the next three numbers in each row?
description: Ten rows of numbers each grow by their own rule. The video writes the next three numbers of every row and checks the triangular row by its jumps.
teaching_notes: One idea: to continue a row, say its rule and apply the rule one step at a time. Watch for students who guess the next numbers without using the rule.

source: Figure it Out Q2 (Math Talk), p.3
video_script.why: The child continues each of ten sequences by three terms, using the rule of the row and not a guess.
video_script.substitution: Say the rule of the row, then apply it one step at a time.
video_script.anchor: the ten rows of number sequences from the book, each with three empty boxes at its end
video_script.payoff_line: Each row grows by its own rule

final_answer.value: Next three numbers: All 1's 1,1,1; Counting 8,9,10; Odd 15,17,19; Even 16,18,20; Triangular 36,45,55; Squares 64,81,100; Cubes 343,512,729; Ziva 34,55,89; Powers of 2 128,256,512; Powers of 3 2187,6561,19683.
final_answer.spoken: every row grows by its own rule, three more terms each

names.Ziva: ancient Indian scholar after whom the sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ... is named

hold_back: Each row grows by its own rule
maths_rules: counting numbers: the last is 7, so 8, 9, 10
odd numbers: the last is 13, so 15, 17, 19; even numbers: the last is 14, so 16, 18, 20
triangular: the last is 28, add 8, 9, 10 to get 36, 45, 55
check: the triangular jumps are 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, so the next jumps are 8, 9, 10 and 28 + 8 = 36
video_script.design: One idea: a rule continues a row. Callback to finding a rule from the jumps. Wrong idea: none is broken. The ten rows stay on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: ones: 1, 1, 1. Counting: after 7 comes 8, 9, 10. Odd: after 13 comes 15, 17, 19. Even: after 14 comes 16, 18, 20

narration: <bookmark mark='ones'/>Step one, the first four rows. The row of ones goes on with one, one, one.
<bookmark mark='count'/>The counting numbers end at seven, so they go on with eight, nine, ten.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>The odd numbers end at thirteen, so they go on with fifteen, seventeen, nineteen.
<bookmark mark='even'/>The even numbers end at fourteen, so they go on with sixteen, eighteen, twenty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: triangular: after 28 comes 36, 45, 55. Squares: 8 x 8 = 64, 9 x 9 = 81, 10 x 10 = 100. Cubes: 7 x 7 x 7 = 343, 8 x 8 x 8 = 512, 9 x 9 x 9 = 729

marks.tri: the boxes of the triangular row are filled
marks.sq: the boxes of the squares row are filled
marks.cube: the boxes of the cubes row are filled

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, the next three rows. The triangular row ends at twenty eight. It goes on with thirty six, forty five, fifty five.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The squares go on with eight times eight, nine times nine and ten times ten. These are sixty four, eighty one and one hundred.
<bookmark mark='cube'/>The cubes go on with seven times seven times seven, and so on. These are three hundred forty three, five hundred twelve and seven hundred twenty nine.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the row named after Ziva: 13 + 21 = 34, 21 + 34 = 55, 34 + 55 = 89. Powers of 2: 64 doubled is 128, then 256, then 512

marks.vira: the first box of the row named after Ziva is filled
marks.vira2: the other two boxes of that row are filled
marks.two: the boxes of the powers of 2 row are filled

narration: <bookmark mark='vira'/>Step three, the next two rows. In the row named after Ziva, thirteen plus twenty one is thirty four.
<bookmark mark='vira2'/>Then twenty one plus thirty four is fifty five. Thirty four plus fifty five is eighty nine.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The powers of two double each time. Sixty four goes on to one hundred twenty eight, two hundred fifty six and five hundred twelve.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: powers of 3: 729 x 3 = 2187, then 6561, then 19683

marks.three: the first box of the powers of 3 row is filled
marks.three2: the other two boxes of that row are filled

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step four, the last row. The powers of three triple each time. Seven hundred twenty nine goes on to two thousand one hundred eighty seven.
<bookmark mark='three2'/>Then comes six thousand five hundred sixty one. After that comes nineteen thousand six hundred eighty three.

beats.on_screen: Check, the triangular row: the jumps 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 go on with 8, 9, 10, and 28 + 8 = 36

marks.check: the triangular row is written with its jumps

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the triangular row by its jumps. The jumps so far are two, three, four, five, six and seven.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next jump is eight, and twenty eight plus eight is thirty six, which matches.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Each row grows by its own rule

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each row grows by its own rule, and now every box has its number.
